title: Raksha Bandhan: Multiplication and Equal Groups
seo_title: Multiplication and Equal Groups Class 3 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 7)
standard_code: Class 3, Maths Mela Chapter 7: Raksha Bandhan
standard_text: Multiplication as repeated addition and equal groups; multiplication facts and tables; using multiplication in daily life (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 3)
meta_desc: Class 3 Raksha Bandhan worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 7): equal groups, repeated addition, times tables and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Times tables help you find totals quickly.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 5 rakhis in each of 3 packets: 5 + 5 + 5 = 3 × 5 = 15.
  • Changing the order gives the same answer: 3 × 5 = 5 × 3.

Examples

Example

6 sweets in each of 4 boxes.

4 × 6

Answer: 24 sweets

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the numbers (4 + 6)4 groups of 6 is 6 + 6 + 6 + 6.
Skipping a step when skip countingSay each multiple: 6, 12, 18, 24.

faq.q: Which tables do Class 3 children learn?
faq.a: Tables of 2 to 10, starting with 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10.
Adding the same number again and again, which multiplication does in one step.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 3 groups. Each group has 4 counters. Count by 4s: 4, 8, 12. So 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 2 groups. Each group has 5 counters. Count by 5s: 5, 10. So 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 5 counters. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 × 5 = 20.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 5 groups. Each group has 3 counters. Count by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. So 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 2 groups. Each group has 6 counters. Count by 6s: 6, 12. So 2 × 6 = 12.

items.q: Which number sentence matches this array?
items.e: Count the rows: 2. Count one row: 6. 2 rows of 6 is 2 × 6 = 12. 2 + 6 only adds the two numbers. It does not count the dots.
Count the rows: 3. Count one row: 7. 3 rows of 7 is 3 × 7 = 21. 3 + 7 only adds the two numbers. It does not count the dots.
Count the rows: 4. Count one row: 5. 4 rows of 5 is 4 × 5 = 20. 4 + 5 only adds the two numbers. It does not count the dots.
Count the rows: 5. Count one row: 8. 5 rows of 8 is 5 × 8 = 40. 5 + 8 only adds the two numbers. It does not count the dots.
Count the rows: 3. Count one row: 9. 3 rows of 9 is 3 × 9 = 27. 3 + 9 only adds the two numbers. It does not count the dots.
There are 5 rows of 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. So 5 × 5 = 25.
There are 4 rows of 7. Count by 7s: 7, 14, 21, 28. So 4 × 7 = 28.
There are 2 rows of 9. Count by 9s: 9, 18. So 2 × 9 = 18.
There are 3 rows of 10. Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30. So 3 × 10 = 30.
Turnaround facts have the same answer. 4 × 7 = 28, so 7 × 4 = 28 too.
Turnaround facts have the same answer. 3 × 9 = 27, so 9 × 3 = 27 too.
Turnaround facts have the same answer. 5 × 8 = 40, so 8 × 5 = 40 too.
Turnaround facts have the same answer. 10 × 6 = 60, so 6 × 10 = 60 too.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 7 × 4?
items.e: 4 × 7 is the turnaround of 7 × 4. Both make 28.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 6 × 5?
items.e: 5 × 6 is the turnaround of 6 × 5. Both make 30.

items.q: Which is the same as 6 + 6 + 6 + 6?
items.e: Count the 6s: there are 4 of them. 4 groups of 6 is 4 × 6 = 24.

items.q: Which is the same as 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3?
items.e: Count the 3s: there are 5 of them. 5 groups of 3 is 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: Which is the same as 8 + 8 + 8?
items.e: Count the 8s: there are 3 of them. 3 groups of 8 is 3 × 8 = 24.

items.q: Which is the same as 10 + 10 + 10 + 10?
items.e: Count the 10s: there are 4 of them. 4 groups of 10 is 4 × 10 = 40.

items.q: Which is the same as 7 + 7?
items.e: Count the 7s: there are 2 of them. 2 groups of 7 is 2 × 7 = 14.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 4 × 9?
items.e: 4 × 9 means 4 groups of 9. Add 4 9s: 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 3 × 8?
items.e: 3 × 8 means 3 groups of 8. Add 3 8s: 8 + 8 + 8 = 24.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 5 × 6?
items.e: 5 × 6 means 5 groups of 6. Add 5 6s: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 30.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 6 × 4?
Which has the same answer as 4 × 7?
items.e: You can multiply in any order and get the same answer. 4 × 7 = 28 and 7 × 4 = 28. So 7 × 4 has the same answer.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 2 × 9?
items.e: You can multiply in any order and get the same answer. 2 × 9 = 18 and 9 × 2 = 18. So 9 × 2 has the same answer.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 6 × 5?
items.e: You can multiply in any order and get the same answer. 6 × 5 = 30 and 5 × 6 = 30. So 5 × 6 has the same answer.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 3 × 10?
items.e: You can multiply in any order and get the same answer. 3 × 10 = 30 and 10 × 3 = 30. So 10 × 3 has the same answer.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 8 × 6?
items.e: You can multiply in any order and get the same answer. 8 × 6 = 48 and 6 × 8 = 48. So 6 × 8 has the same answer.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 9 × 4?
items.e: You can multiply in any order and get the same answer. 9 × 4 = 36 and 4 × 9 = 36. So 4 × 9 has the same answer.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 6 × 9 = 9 × ☐
items.e: The order of the numbers can change. The answer stays the same. 6 × 9 = 9 × 6, so the missing number is 6. Both are 54.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 5 × 8 = 8 × ☐
items.e: The order of the numbers can change. The answer stays the same. 5 × 8 = 8 × 5, so the missing number is 5. Both are 40.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 7 × 3 = 3 × ☐
items.e: The order of the numbers can change. The answer stays the same. 7 × 3 = 3 × 7, so the missing number is 7. Both are 21.

items.q: This array shows 3 × 5 = 15. Which other number sentence also matches it?
items.e: Turn the array a quarter turn. 3 rows of 5 become 5 rows of 3. The number of dots does not change, so 5 × 3 = 15.
Turn the array a quarter turn. 4 rows of 6 become 6 rows of 4. The number of dots does not change, so 6 × 4 = 24.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 3. 4 × 3 = 12.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 5 groups of 4. 5 × 4 = 20.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 7 dots in each row. 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 6 dots in each row. 4 × 6 = 24.

items.q: Which number sentence matches this array?
items.e: There are 5 rows with 3 dots in each row, so it shows 5 × 3 = 15. 3 × 5 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q: Which number sentence matches this array?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 8 dots in each row, so it shows 4 × 8 = 32. 8 × 4 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q:
Skip count by 3s. What comes next?
12, 15, 18, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 18 + 3 = 21. So 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q:
Skip count by 4s. What comes next?
20, 24, 28, ?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before: 28 + 4 = 32. So 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: 2 × 7 = 14. Double it to find 4 × 7.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 7 is double 2 × 7: 14 + 14 = 28.

items.q: 2 × 9 = 18. Double it to find 4 × 9.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 9 is double 2 × 9: 18 + 18 = 36.

items.q:
Skip count by 5s. What comes next?
15, 20, 25, ?
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 25 + 5 = 30. So 5 × 6 = 30.

items.q:
Skip count by 10s. What comes next?
40, 50, 60, ?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before: 60 + 10 = 70. So 10 × 7 = 70.

items.q: 10 × 6 = 60. Use it to find 5 × 6.
items.e: 5 is half of 10, so 5 × 6 is half of 10 × 6. Half of 60 is 30.

items.q: 10 × 8 = 80. Use it to find 5 × 8.
items.e: 5 is half of 10, so 5 × 8 is half of 10 × 8. Half of 80 is 40.

items.q: 10 × 3 = 30. Use it to find 5 × 3.
items.e: 5 is half of 10, so 5 × 3 is half of 10 × 3. Half of 30 is 15.
10 × 7 = 70. The 5s are half of the 10s: half of 70 is 35.
10 × 4 = 40. The 5s are half of the 10s: half of 40 is 20.
10 × 2 = 20. The 5s are half of the 10s: half of 20 is 10.
6 tens make 60. So 6 × 10 = 60.
4 tens make 40. So 4 × 10 = 40.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 3. 6 × 3 = 18.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 9 dots in each row. 3 × 9 = 27.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 5 rows with 3 dots in each row, so it shows 5 × 3 = 15. 3 × 5 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 3 dots in each row, so it shows 4 × 3 = 12. 3 × 4 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

Count in 3s. What comes next?
9, 12, 15, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 15 + 3 = 18. So 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q:

21, 24, 27, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 27 + 3 = 30. So 3 × 10 = 30.

items.q:

27, 30, 33, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 33 + 3 = 36. So 3 × 12 = 36.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 7 groups of 4. 7 × 4 = 28.

items.q: 2 × 12 = 24. Double it to find 4 × 12.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 12 is double 2 × 12: 24 + 24 = 48.

items.q:
Count in 4s. What comes next?
16, 20, 24, ?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before: 24 + 4 = 28. So 4 × 7 = 28.

items.q:
Count in 4s. What comes next?
28, 32, 36, ?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before: 36 + 4 = 40. So 4 × 10 = 40.
Double 10, then double again: 10 → 20 → 40.
Double 6, then double again: 6 → 12 → 24.
Double 7, then double again: 7 → 14 → 28.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 3 groups of 8. 3 × 8 = 24.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 5 groups of 8. 5 × 8 = 40.

items.q: 4 × 6 = 24. Double it to find 8 × 6.
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 6 is double 4 × 6: 24 + 24 = 48.

items.q: 4 × 3 = 12. Double it to find 8 × 3.
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 3 is double 4 × 3: 12 + 12 = 24.

items.q: 4 × 11 = 44. Double it to find 8 × 11.
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 11 is double 4 × 11: 44 + 44 = 88.

items.q:
Count in 8s. What comes next?
8, 16, 24, ?
items.e: Each number is 8 more than the one before: 24 + 8 = 32. So 8 × 4 = 32.

items.q: A tricycle has 3 wheels. Nisha sees 6 tricycles at the preschool. How many wheels is that?
items.e: 6 tricycles with 3 wheels each: 6 × 3 = 18. 9 is 6 + 3, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: A chair has 4 legs. How many legs do 9 chairs have?
items.e: 9 × 4 = 36. Double 9 is 18, double 18 is 36.

items.q: Yoghurt tubs come in packs of 4. Priya’s mother buys 7 packs. How many tubs is that?
items.e: 7 packs of 4: 7 × 4 = 28. Double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28.

items.q: Manav has six ₹5 notes. How much money does he have?
items.e: 6 × ₹5 = ₹30. ₹11 is 6 + 5, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: Each student has 10 fingers. 7 students hold up all their fingers. How many fingers is that?
A basketball team has 5 players on the court. There are 6 teams at the sports carnival. How many players is that?
At the sausage sizzle, each tray holds 10 sausages. There are 8 trays. How many sausages is that?
Students sit in groups of 3 for maths. There are 8 groups. How many students is that?
items.e: 8 groups of 3: 8 × 3 = 24. 21 is only 7 groups.

items.q: There are 24 wheels on some tricycles. How many tricycles are there?
items.e: Each tricycle has 3 wheels. 24 ÷ 3 = ? 3 × 8 = 24, so there are 8 tricycles.

items.q: 35 students get into teams of 5 for sport. How many teams are there?
items.e: 35 ÷ 5 = ? Think 5 × ? = 35. 5 × 7 = 35, so there are 7 teams.

items.q: The class sets up chairs in the gym. There are 6 rows. Each row has 8 chairs. How many chairs are there?
items.e: There are 6 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 6 × 8 = 48. Adding 6 + 8 = 14 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: A pack of hockey cards has 8 cards. Siddharth buys 4 packs. How many cards does he get?
items.e: There are 4 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 4 × 8 = 32. Adding 4 + 8 = 12 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: At camp, 7 canoes go out on the lake. Each canoe holds 3 people. How many people can the canoes hold?
items.e: There are 7 equal groups of 3, so multiply: 7 × 3 = 21. Adding 7 + 3 = 10 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Sneha skates 4 laps around the rink each day. How many laps does she skate in 7 days?
items.e: There are 7 equal groups of 4, so multiply: 7 × 4 = 28. Adding 7 + 4 = 11 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Each ringette team has 6 players on the ice. 4 teams line up on the ice for a photo. How many players is that?
items.e: There are 4 equal groups of 6, so multiply: 4 × 6 = 24. Adding 4 + 6 = 10 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: At lunch, 8 students sit at each table. There are 9 full tables. How many students are at the tables?
items.e: There are 9 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 9 × 8 = 72. Adding 9 + 8 = 17 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Arjun shares 36 hockey cards equally among 4 friends. How many cards does each friend get?
items.e: Sharing among 4 friends: 36 ÷ 4. 4 × 9 = 36, so each friend gets 9 cards.

items.q: In gym class, 30 students make teams of 5. How many teams are there?
items.e: Grouping in 5s: 30 ÷ 5. 5 × 6 = 30, so there are 6 teams.

items.q: There are 56 chairs in the gym. They are in 7 equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?
items.e: 56 chairs in 7 equal rows: 56 ÷ 7. 7 × 8 = 56, so each row has 8 chairs.

items.q: 32 students go on a field trip. Each parent driver takes 4 students. How many cars are needed?
items.e: Groups of 4: 32 ÷ 4. 4 × 8 = 32, so 8 cars are needed.
